title.rendered: Blessed Are the Merciful: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy.” A morning devotional on the mercy that flows back to those who give it away.

content.rendered:
There is a certain kind of person you meet only rarely. Someone who has been through terrible things and yet, somehow, has come out the other side with a heart softer, not harder. Jesus said that kind of heart is blessed.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, September 1, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Blessed are the merciful, For they shall obtain mercy.”
Matthew 5:7 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

There is a certain kind of person you meet only rarely. Someone who has been through terrible things and yet, somehow, has come out the other side with a heart softer, not harder. When they hear another person’s story, they lean in rather than pull back. When they see someone stumbling, they extend a hand rather than a lecture. When they are wronged, they respond with a grace that costs them something. When you are around them, something in you relaxes. You have found a merciful heart. And Jesus said that kind of heart is blessed.

The setting for Jesus’ declaration is the Sermon on the Mount, the opening address of His public ministry. He climbs a hillside in Galilee, sits down as any rabbi would to teach, and begins with the beatitudes, a list of the kinds of people the Kingdom of God actually calls blessed. Fifth on that list, He names the merciful. “Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.”

The Greek word Jesus uses is eleēmōn. It carries the sense of mercy that has skin in the game of what it sees. Not pity from a safe distance. Not sentiment expressed by a nod. Active, engaged mercy that steps toward the suffering it sees and does something. The Passion Translation renders it: “How enriched you are when you demonstrate tender mercy! For tender mercy will be demonstrated to you” (Matthew 5:7 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Blessed (happy, to be envied, and spiritually prosperous—with life-joy and satisfaction in God’s favor and salvation, regardless of their outward conditions) are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy!” (Matthew 5:7 AMPC).

Jesus then adds the promise that has echoed through the whole Christian tradition. The merciful shall obtain mercy. In the Kingdom Jesus is unveiling, the currency you spend on others is the currency you receive from the Father. That does not mean mercy earns salvation. Salvation is a gift, purchased entirely at the cross. But the person who has genuinely received the mercy of God tends to become a person who genuinely extends the mercy of God. And the person who extends the mercy of God tends to find more of the mercy of God flowing back to them from the Father, from other people, from the atmosphere of their own life. Mercy given and mercy received are woven together in the economy of the Kingdom.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the practical invitation of the beatitude. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, there is someone in your life today who needs mercy from you. Someone who has hurt you. Someone who is struggling. Someone who has failed. Someone who is stumbling. Choose mercy today. Not because they deserve it, but because you have received it. And the promise of the beatitude is that the mercy you give will not leave your life poorer. It will draw more of the mercy of God back into your own daily walk. The merciful are blessed. The merciful shall obtain mercy. Walk in it today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I have received Your mercy without deserving it. Every day of my life is held together by Your mercy in Christ. Today I choose to be a channel of that same mercy to the people around me. I refuse to nurse offence. I refuse to hold grudges. I refuse to withhold what You have freely given to me. I extend Your mercy today to the ones who have hurt me, to the ones who are struggling, to the ones who have failed. And I trust Your promise that the mercy I give will not leave my life poorer, but will draw more of Your mercy back into my walk. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I have received the mercy of God in Christ. Today I extend that same mercy to the people around me. The merciful are blessed. I walk in mercy today, given and received.

  • Micah 6:8 (NKJV): To do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God
